source_locator: R1947: renamed I./Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 on 24 June 1944 / R1938: I./Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 formed 24 June 1944 at Bayeux with batteries 1-6
notes: Event date: 24 June 1944 (Holm, day date). Event definition: the battalion was re-formed in the Bayeux area on this date. Event support: one source family (Holm, ww2.dk; two pages). Location: Bayeux (place PL0033) with a precision of 10 km (the place point has 1 km; the claim uses 10 km because the source's "Bayeux" is read as the Bayeux area, G9). Location support: Holm names Bayeux. Review: confidence 0.3 from the rubric (G-b/L7/G9: area given by one named town, recorded at the town with 10 km precision (0.3)); added in the Luftwaffe ground G-b pass (branch normandy-lw-ground-b, 19 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations). Context: The renaming is an alternate name (G3), not a new unit. Changed in the Luftwaffe ground G-b follow-up (branch normandy-lw-ground-b, 19 November 2026): confidence old value 0.5, new value 0.3; precision_km old value 5, new value 10; location_basis old value documented_on_date, new value operational_area; reason: Bayeux was in Allied hands from 7 June 1944, so Holm's "Bayeux" for the re-formation on 24 June is read as the Bayeux area, not the town (G9: one named town at 10 km, 0.3); Scott accepted G-b Q5, 19 November 2026. Holm's Abteilung page has batteries 5 and 6 of battalion 266 under 13. Flak-Division on 1 June and 1 July 1944 (note). [FMS B-597 (branch fms-b597, 23 November 2026): Disagreement (no value changed): B-597 (the 20 September 1944 corps report, p.-4-, Fold3 page 106; ms -34-, Fold3 page 87) has Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 detached from the corps in the area west of Bayeux at the start of the invasion (C12781), rejoining the corps only several weeks (mehrere Wochen) later; it gives no place on 24 June 1944. Bayeux was in British hands from 7 June 1944 (C0044), so Holm's 24 June Bayeux stays read as the area behind the German line; values left as they are and rechecked under roadmap 422 (Scott accepted B-597 Q8, 23 November 2026).]
